title: Introduction to function overloading
recap: An overload set contains functions sharing a name but accepting different parameter types. A call selects an overload from its argument types, letting one operation have appropriately typed implementations.
Return type alone cannot distinguish two overloads with identical parameter lists. The caller must be able to choose before using the return value.
objectives: Implement the stated behavior for multiple inputs.
Run the visible tests and explain one boundary case.
warnings: The function/type interface is fixed, but implementation syntax is your choice.
Do not remove the visible tests; the checker keeps an independent copy.
Respect the stated input domain and lifetime/range rules.
challenge: Implement both doubleValue overloads: int -> int and double -> double. Each returns twice its argument, preserving the appropriate result type. Integer inputs are at most one million in magnitude. Do not convert the double overload through int.
hints: The double overload needs double arithmetic.
The tests check the result types as part of the public API.
